dhpak2.6:1.1: The English story title aligns with the Pāli story title. The romanized title Pamattāpamattadvesahāyakabhikkhūnaṁ was removed because it has no separate corresponding passage.
dhpak2.6:3.1: The editorial heading ‘Utter Heedlessness’ was removed because it has no separate corresponding passage in the local Pāli story.
dhpak2.6:3.3: daharasāmaṇerehi identifies young novices, not ‘young bhikkhus and novices.’ visibbamāno says the idle bhikkhu warmed himself while chatting during the first watch; the opening English account had omitted this action.
dhpak2.6:3.5: cattāro apāyā names the four lower realms, not merely ‘four states of suffering.’
dhpak2.6:3.8: The Pāli says the heedful bhikkhu spoke no further to his friend (taṃ avatvā); the English had said he failed to spur him to greater effort.
dhpak2.6:3.9: Itaro ‘nāyaṃ vacanakkhamo’ti taṃ avatvā appamattova samaṇadhammamakāsi says he continued his practice without speaking further to his friend; the English had said he resumed meditation.
dhpak2.6:4.2: itarassa caṅkamitvā gabbhaṃ paviṭṭhakāle pavisitvā does not specify that the slothful elder entered the monastery; the English had supplied that destination.
dhpak2.6:4.5: samaṇadhammaṃ means the broader practice of a renunciant, not meditation alone.
dhpak2.6:4.7: Itaropi majjhimayāme vissamitvā says the heedful bhikkhu rested during the middle watch and rose in the last; the English had placed his walking in the first watch here, though the Pāli mentions it earlier.
dhpak2.6:4.8: samaṇadhammaṃ means the broader practice of a renunciant, not meditation alone.
dhpak2.6:5.1: Te vuṭṭhavassā places their visit to the Teacher after the rains retreat; the English had called this only ‘completed residence.’
dhpak2.6:5.4: samaṇadhammaṃ means the broader practice of a renunciant, not meditation alone.
dhpak2.6:6.2: appamattaṃ pana pamattaṃ karosi says the idle bhikkhu calls the heedful one heedless, not ‘You mistake heedlessness for heedfulness.’
dhpak2.6:7.1: The Teacher's connective statement about explaining the danger of heedlessness and the benefits of heedfulness is Pāli-only under this key.
dhpak2.6:8.1: javacchinno dubbalasso is a weak horse that has lost its speed; the English had called it a ‘decrepit hack.’ The editorial heading ‘Like a Recer’ was removed.
dhpak2.6:8.2: sīghajavasso is a swift horse; the English had called it a ‘racer.’
dhpak2.6:9.1: The repeated Pāli transcription of verse 29 was removed because it has no separate corresponding passage in the local Pāli story.
dhpak2.6:10.1: The full Pāli explanation of verse 29 has no English translation and remains Pāli-only under this paragraph.
dhpak2.6:11.1: The appended ‘377:’ note was removed because it has no separate corresponding passage in the local Pāli story.
dhpak2.6:12.1: The Pāli closing title Pamattāpamattadvesahāyakavatthu chaṭṭhaṃ is Pāli-only and has no English key.
